description:
pkix-ct/src/lib.rs:67-167

`Error::ParseError` is returned for:

- Invalid SCT-list DER (sct.rs:159)
- OCSP response DER (delivery.rs:75-81)
- BasicOcspResponse DER (delivery.rs:80-81)
- JSON syntax errors in log_list.json (log_list.rs:194)
- Base64 in `log_id` or `key` (log_list.rs:198, 203)
- Length-mismatch on `log_id` decode (log_list.rs:202)
- RFC 3339 timestamp parse (log_list.rs:243-256)
- log_id ⇔ key SHA-256 mismatch (log_list.rs:83)
- x509-cert parse failure (verify.rs:964, 1006)
- DER re-encode failure (verify.rs:985, 1012)
- TBS-too-long after re-encode (verify.rs:986-988)

11 distinct underlying causes collapse into one `ParseError`. A
caller debugging a malformed log_list.json file cannot tell which
sub-element was malformed (timestamp? base64? log_id length?).

`Error::TruncatedOrTrailing` is similarly multi-cause: short SCT,
short SCT list, short u16-prefix payload, trailing bytes after
declared length.

This is information leakage in the SOURCE direction: the verifier
DROPS information from the dep's error types when mapping into
`Error::ParseError`. The contract becomes "anything could have gone
wrong; you cannot tell which".

Recommendation: take advantage of std's error chain. Behind the
`std` feature, store `Box<dyn std::error::Error + Send + Sync>` as
an optional `source` and implement `source()`:

```rust
#[cfg(feature = "std")]
impl std::error::Error for Error {
    fn source(&self) -> Option<&(dyn std::error::Error + 'static)> {
        match self {
            Error::ParseError => None,  // or stored cause
            ...
        }
    }
}
```

Or, simpler: add a `Cause` variant struct with a small string
describing the location of the failure ("oid 1.3.6.1.4.1.11129.2.4.5
extension value", "log_id base64 decode", etc.). String is cheap;
it's information that the caller can include in their own
diagnostics.

Or split `Error::ParseError` into:
- `Error::SctListMalformed`
- `Error::OcspResponseMalformed`
- `Error::LogListMalformed { field: &'static str }`
- `Error::CertMalformed`
- `Error::DerEncodingFailure`

Priority P2: callers operating in production WILL see ParseError in
the wild and need to triage. Today they cannot.
title: Error variants do not capture inner causes (no #[source]) — collapses 5 distinct failure modes into ParseError
